result.title: On the Difficulty of Sequence-Level Supervised Learning for Autoregressive Language Models
result.summary: During the supervised learning phase, autoregressive language models are typically trained by minimizing the negative log-likelihood of the training data, which decomposes as a sum of token-level cross-entropies via teacher forcing. This objective is simple and efficient but potentially suffers from so-called exposure bias: a mismatch between the way the model is trained and the way it is used at inference time. Can we instead design sequence-level loss functions that incorporate inference-time decoding procedures, such as greedy decoding or autoregressive sampling? We show that two natural attempts lead to loss functions that are fundamentally flawed: unbounded below. We further show that these two flawed loss functions are intimately connected: using autoregressive Gumbel tricks, the sampling based loss is the expected greedy loss under Gumbel perturbations. Since the pathology stems from the dependence of the decoded sequence on the model parameters, we analyze the update direction obtained by applying a stop gradient on the sampling procedure, leading to a moment matching direction. While it is not the gradient of any loss function, we prove that it defines a valid descent direction in function space for the autoregressive negative log-likelihood. Despite these theoretical insights, the moment matching direction suffers from high variance. We conclude that teacher forcing may well be ``all you need'' for supervised learning of autoregressive models.

AI.brief_summary: 该文分析自回归语言模型采用序列级监督的困难，指出引入贪心解码或采样的两类自然损失下界无界，并借助 Gumbel 技巧与 stop-gradient 分析其更新方向及高方差问题，最终主张 teacher forcing 可能已足够。
AI.relevance_reason: 其关于解码过程进入损失、曝光偏差和采样梯度高方差的讨论，可供核查 LVR 中轨迹式训练、监督信号与贡献分配的稳定性，但并未直接涉及视觉或多模态推理状态。
